title: Invariance of relative simplicial homotopy classes under target equivalence
statement: Use simplicial sets, products, quasicategories, Kan complexes and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. All objects fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $A\subseteq B$ be a simplicial subset, $u:X\to Y$ a simplicial map, and $a:A\to X$ a simplicial map. Let $[B,X]_a$ denote maps $f:B\to X$ restricting exactly to $a$, modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs admitting a map $H:B\times\Delta^1\to X$ with those endpoints and $H|_{A\times\Delta^1}=a\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$. Define $[B,Y]_{ua}$ in the same way. In either of the following two cases, postcomposition induces a bijection $u_*:[B,X]_a\xrightarrow{\sim}[B,Y]_{ua}$: (i) $X,Y$ are Kan complexes and $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, with no restriction on $A$; (ii) $X,Y$ are quasicategories, $u$ is a categorical equivalence, and $A$ contains every vertex of $B$. Empty extension sets and $A=B$ are allowed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 1.2.7.3(2) and Proposition 1.2.5.3 (equivalences on functor categories and their cores), with the strict-fiber argument for restriction. Restriction is an isofibration by Kerodon Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3), and equivalences in a functor category are detected at vertices. For Kan targets the restriction map is a Kan fibration. Apply Kerodon Proposition 3.2.8.1 (00XC) to the restriction square of Kan complexes (cores in case (ii)). The all-vertices condition identifies its strict fiber with the relative diagrams in (ii). These are the precise ingredients of the stated corollary, not a verbatim assertion of one HTT proposition. Read online 2026-10-17; no archived HTT/Kerodon copy in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy assertion.

proof.text: For $K=A,B$ and $Z=X,Y$ put $D_{K,Z}=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$ and $M_{K,Z}=D_{K,Z}^{\simeq}$. These functor objects are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory]; in case (i) they are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], so $M_{K,Z}=D_{K,Z}$ by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. In both cases restriction $D_{B,Z}\to D_{A,Z}$ is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], hence $r_Z:M_{B,Z}\to M_{A,Z}$ is a Kan fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. The $M_{K,Z}$ are themselves Kan: $D_{K,Z}\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration (inner horns fill and the identity equivalence lifts degenerately), so the same core-fibration statement applied to this map gives the Kan lifting property. All these objects fit in the fixed universe.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3), Proposition 4.4.3.7 (01EZ), and Corollary 3.1.3.4 (00TN); HTT Proposition 1.2.7.3(1).

proof.text: In case (i), [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] gives a simplicial inverse $v:Y\to X$ up to prisms $H:X\times\Delta^1\to X$ and $J:Y\times\Delta^1\to Y$, with endpoints $vu,\mathrm{id}_X$ and $uv,\mathrm{id}_Y$. For any $K$, exponentiate these prisms explicitly: an $n$-simplex $F:K\times\Delta^n\to X$ and $t:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$ are sent to the map $(k,s)\mapsto H(F(k,s),t(s))$; for $F:K\times\Delta^n\to Y$, the second prism sends $(F,t)$ to $(k,s)\mapsto J(F(k,s),t(s))$. These formulas commute with simplicial operators and have endpoints $v_*u_*,\mathrm{id}$ and $u_*v_*,\mathrm{id}$. Thus [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] makes $u_*:D_{K,X}\to D_{K,Y}$ a weak homotopy equivalence. By step 1 this is the required comparison $M_{K,X}\to M_{K,Y}$, for $K=A,B$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13 (00UB), using Corollary 3.6.4.3 (03X7) for the realization convention; explicit exponentiation of cylinder homotopies.

proof.text: In case (ii), apply clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] to $u$. It supplies a simplicial map $v:Y\to X$ and coherent natural equivalences between $vu$ and $\mathrm{id}_X$, and between $uv$ and $\mathrm{id}_Y$. In the quasicategories $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Y)$ (quasicategories by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory]), each such edge gives an isomorphism in the edge-and-triangle category $h$: its two inverse triangles become the two inverse equations. Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval] to these pairs of vertices. With $I=N(\mathcal J)$ for the two-object groupoid specified there, this gives maps $I\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$ and $I\to\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Y)$ with the specified endpoints. Evaluation gives $T:X\times I\to X$ and $S:Y\times I\to Y$ with endpoints $vu,\mathrm{id}_X$ and $uv,\mathrm{id}_Y$. We only need these endpoints, not equality with the originally chosen equivalence edges.

source.place: Remark 3.6.5 and Corollary 3.6.6, printed p.114, and Theorem 3.6.8, printed pp.115-116; the equivalence/J-homotopy argument.

proof.text: For $K=A,B$, exponentiate $T$ to $T_K:D_{K,X}\times I\to D_{K,X}$ by the degreewise formula $T_K(F,j)(k,s)=T(F(k,s),j(s))$, and exponentiate $S$ to $S_K:D_{K,Y}\times I\to D_{K,Y}$ by $S_K(G,j)(k,s)=S(G(k,s),j(s))$. Each postcomposition functor preserves equivalence edges: applying a simplicial map to an inverse edge and its two inverse triangles preserves those witnesses. For $(Z,R)=(X,T_K)$ or $(Y,S_K)$, this also shows that $R$ restricts to $M_{K,Z}\times I\to M_{K,Z}$: an edge in the first factor has an inverse with inverse triangles since that factor is Kan by step 1, and an edge in $I$ has its groupoid inverse and the nerve triangles; pairing the witnesses gives inverse triangles in the product. Its image under $R$ is therefore an equivalence, so every simplex has all its image edges in the core. Restricting along the map $\Delta^1\to I$ defined by $0\to1$ gives $T_K|_{M_{K,X}\times\Delta^1}$ with endpoints $v_*u_*,\mathrm{id}_{M_{K,X}}$, and $S_K|_{M_{K,Y}\times\Delta^1}$ with endpoints $u_*v_*,\mathrm{id}_{M_{K,Y}}$. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], the specified map $u_*:M_{K,X}\to M_{K,Y}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The facts about inverses in a Kan complex used here are in [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration].

source.place: Agent expansion of the core-invariance observation following Proposition 1.2.5.3 and the postcomposition argument of Proposition 1.2.7.3(2); all factorization through cores is checked using inverse triangles.

proof.text: In both cases the square with horizontal maps $u_*:M_{B,X}\to M_{B,Y}$ and $u_*:M_{A,X}\to M_{A,Y}$ and vertical maps $r_X,r_Y$ commutes strictly: both composites restrict a diagram to $A$ and then apply $u$. Use the cospans $M_{B,X}\xrightarrow{r_X}M_{A,X}\xleftarrow{}\{a\}$ and $M_{B,Y}\xrightarrow{r_Y}M_{A,Y}\xleftarrow{}\{ua\}$. Their comparison maps are weak homotopy equivalences by steps 2 or 4 and the isomorphism of singleton simplicial sets, and their left legs are Kan fibrations by step 1. Hence [lem-coef-kan-pullback-fibration-invariance] gives a weak homotopy equivalence $u_*:P_X\to P_Y$ of the strict fibers over $a$ and $ua$. These fibers are Kan directly by lifting a horn in $M_{B,Z}$ over the constant simplex of $M_{A,Z}$ using $r_Z$; this also permits empty fibers.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.2 (0109); applied to the two restriction cospans with a singleton boundary point.

proof.text: For $(Z,c)=(X,a)$ and $(Y,ua)$, all vertices of $D_{B,Z}$ belong to its core, so the vertices of $P_Z$ are exactly extensions $f:B\to Z$ of $c$. In case (i) the functor objects equal their cores, so edges of these fibers are exactly the prisms fixed on $A\times\Delta^1$ in the statement. In case (ii), any such prism $H$ has at each vertex $b$ of $B$ the degenerate edge at $c(b)$, because $b\in A$; this is an equivalence (the degenerate triangles witness its inverse). Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with $K=B$: $H$ is an equivalence edge of $D_{B,Z}$ and therefore belongs to its core. Its restriction is the degenerate edge at $c$, so it is an edge of $P_Z$. Conversely every edge of $P_Z$ is a prism with exactly this boundary restriction by the definition of the strict fiber. Thus the two relative equivalence relations are precisely those generated by fiber edges. Postcomposition sends a relative prism $H$ to $u\circ H$, whose boundary is $(ua)\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$, so it induces the specified map on both generated equivalence relations.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK); the all-vertices hypothesis is used only to identify the relative prism relation with core-fiber edges.

proof.text: For any simplicial set $P$, vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by its edges identify with path components of $|P|$: every point of a realized simplex joins a vertex by a straight segment, and all vertices of that simplex join along its edges. Conversely, send a point in a simplex to the edge-component of any of its vertices. This is independent of the chosen vertex and of face/degeneracy representatives, and is continuous to the discrete set of edge-components by the quotient definition of realization in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], since it is constant on each summand simplex. A path cannot join different values. This proves the identification naturally in $P$. A weak homotopy equivalence induces a bijection on path components by that same definition. Apply this to step 5 and then use step 6: the resulting bijection is exactly postcomposition $[B,X]_a\to[B,Y]_{ua}$. If a fiber is empty the component argument is still valid; if $A=B$ each fiber is the singleton prescribed diagram; if $B$ is empty both relative class sets are singletons.
